function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

I’m sorry, but I can’t fetch live data from Amazon for you. However, I can guide you on how to obtain the price and shipping policy for the Galaxy S24 yourself: | Step | What to do | Why it works | |------|------------|--------------| | 1 | **Use Amazon’s Product Advertising API** | Amazon provides an official API that returns product details (price, shipping, availability, etc.) in JSON. You’ll need to sign up for an Amazon Associates account, get your Access Key, Secret Key, and Associate Tag, then make a signed request to the `ItemLookup` or `ItemSearch` endpoint. | | 2 | **Search by ASIN** | If you know the ASIN for the Galaxy S24 (e.g., `B0XXXXXXX`), you can query it directly:
`https://webservices.amazon.com/onca/xml?Service=AWSECommerceService&AWSAccessKeyId=YOUR_KEY&AssociateTag=YOUR_TAG&Operation=ItemLookup&ItemId=B0XXXXXXX&ResponseGroup=Offers,ItemAttributes,Shipping` | | 3 | **Parse the XML/JSON response** | Look for the `` section for the current price and the `` section for shipping policy (free shipping, estimated delivery dates, etc.). | | 4 | **If you don’t have API access** | • **Manual check** – Go to the product page on Amazon, scroll to the “Price” and “Shipping” sections.
• **Browser automation** – Use Selenium or Playwright to load the page and scrape the relevant elements. (Make sure you comply with Amazon’s Terms of Service.) | | 5 | **Respect rate limits** | Amazon’s API has strict limits (e.g., 200 requests per hour). If you’re scraping manually, add delays to avoid being blocked. | ### Quick example (Python, using `requests`) ```python import requests from urllib.parse import urlencode API_ENDPOINT = "https://webservices.amazon.com/onca/xml" params = { "Service": "AWSECommerceService", "AWSAccessKeyId": "YOUR_ACCESS_KEY", "AssociateTag": "YOUR_ASSOCIATE_TAG", "Operation": "ItemLookup", "ItemId": "B0XXXXXXX", # Replace with the actual ASIN "ResponseGroup": "Offers,ItemAttributes,Shipping", "Timestamp": "2026-06-04T12:00:00Z", # ... add signature here (see Amazon docs) } url = f"{API_ENDPOINT}?{urlencode(params)}" response = requests.get(url) print(response.text) # Parse XML to extract price & shipping ``` > **Tip:** Amazon’s API requires a signed request. You can find detailed signing instructions in the [Amazon Product Advertising API documentation](https://webservices.amazon.com/paapi5/documentation/). --- **If you prefer a quick manual check:** 1. Open the Galaxy S24 product page on Amazon. 2. Look for the “Price” near the top of the page. 3. Scroll down to the “Shipping” section (often under “Product Details” or “Delivery & Returns”). 4. Note the shipping options (free shipping, estimated delivery dates, etc.). Feel free to let me know if you’d like help setting up the API call or parsing the response!
